prompt: Build chord names like "Ctrl+Shift+S" from e.getModifiersEx() and e.getKeyCode() in keyPressed, ignoring presses of the modifier keys themselves.
explanation: getModifiersEx() packs the held modifiers into one int, so you test a single modifier by masking with & and comparing against 0 -- never with == to the mask alone, since several bits can be set at once. Building the name with a fixed prefix order keeps "Ctrl+Shift+S" stable no matter which key the user pressed first. Skipping VK_SHIFT and VK_CONTROL matters because holding a modifier delivers its own keyPressed event before the real key arrives.
hints: (e.getModifiersEx() & KeyEvent.SHIFT_DOWN_MASK) != 0 is the test for shift being held; CTRL_DOWN_MASK is the same idea.
Return early from keyPressed when e.getKeyCode() is VK_SHIFT or VK_CONTROL, before doing anything else.
Start with an empty string, append "Ctrl+" then "Shift+" as needed, and finish with KeyEvent.getKeyText(e.getKeyCode()).
